title: AI-generated web page usability diagnose loop
description:
# AI-generated web page usability diagnose loop

## Intent

As a publication or product operator shipping AI-generated or AI-assisted
web pages (landing pages, article layouts, dashboards, artifact-style UI),
I want the same diagnose/decide/apply/verify loop PPY-54055d built for
prose, applied to a rendered page instead: a read-only scanner that
surfaces concrete, steerable usability findings, not an auto-fixer.

Sibling capability under Limatus, not a rewrite of the editorial loop.
Same shape, same guardrails, different artifact: a page instead of a
paragraph.

## Guardrail (non-negotiable, carried over from PPY-54055d)

Findings are signal. The scanner never silently rewrites markup, CSS, or
copy on the page. A human (or an agent exercising real judgment, not
pattern-matching) still decides skip / rewrite / delete / keep per
finding, same as the editorial loop. No auto-apply, ever, for anything
that touches a published page.

## Why this is a genuinely different problem, not the same one restyled

Prose redundancy and web usability are not the same kind of defect, and
treating them as interchangeable would produce a shallow tool:

- Prose findings are almost entirely textual pattern matches (shingle
  overlap, banned lexicon, passive voice). Usability findings are largely
  structural/visual: contrast ratios, tap-target size, focus order,
  whether a CTA is reachable, whether an information hierarchy matches
  the content's actual priority. Some of that is measurable from
  rendered DOM/CSS; some of it needs an actual look at the page.
- The editorial loop's "false positive" lesson has a direct analog: a
  deliberately sparse, minimal page is not the same defect as an
  unfinished one, and a scanner tuned only on "more elements = more
  polish" will punish restraint. Whatever house-style equivalent exists
  for pages needs to encode that the way style-profile.yml's
  voicePatterns/bannedPatterns encode it for prose.
- "AI-generated page" slop has its own recognizable tells, distinct from
  prose slop: generic gradient hero + centered everything + the same
  three-icon feature row, ungrounded stock-photo hero imagery,
  emoji-as-section-marker, an accent color fighting itself across
  components. Some of this already exists as qualitative guidance
  (artifact-design's "avoid AI-generated design" list); this epic is
  about making a checkable subset of it into scanner findings the way
  editorial diagnose made prose slop checkable.

## Candidate finding categories (draft, not committed)

- Accessibility-adjacent: contrast ratio, tap-target size, missing
  alt/focus states -- most mechanically checkable, likely ships first.
- Structural/layout: viewport overflow, broken responsive behavior,
  inconsistent spacing rhythm, orphaned or unreachable interactive
  elements.
- Generic-template tells: the visual-design equivalent of banned prose
  lexicon -- the palette/type/layout clichés that read as generated
  rather than considered.
- Content/UX mismatch: CTA that doesn't match the page's stated goal,
  navigation that dead-ends, a form with no visible error state.

## Open questions

- Input artifact: rendered HTML+CSS, a live URL, a screenshot, or some
  combination? Contrast/tap-target checks want computed styles; "does
  this read as considered" checks may want a screenshot and a real look.
- Own profile schema (a design-system equivalent of style-profile.yml),
  or extend the same schema with a visual/structural rules block?
- Where does off-the-shelf accessibility tooling (axe-core, Lighthouse)
  end and genuinely new judgment begin? Don't rebuild what those already
  do well -- the value-add is the steerable, house-aware judgment layer
  on top, same way editorial diagnose doesn't reinvent a spell-checker.
- Does "apply" mean the same thing here as for prose? Would a human ever
  want a generated CSS patch auto-applied the way a rewrite option is,
  or does this loop stop at diagnose + steer for the visual side?

## Out of scope for now

- Auto-applying any visual/layout fix without human review -- same rule
  as the editorial loop, doubled: a bad prose edit is embarrassing, a
  bad CSS auto-apply can break a live page.
- Rebuilding general-purpose accessibility auditing from scratch.
- A generalized visual-regression/screenshot-diff system -- this is
  about usability judgment, not pixel-diffing.

## Relationship to the rest of Limatus

Sibling epic under PPY-809091, alongside PPY-54055d (editorial loop),
PPY-639fb3 (CLI/SDK decoupling), PPY-89827a (evals), and PPY-b536c2
(Papyrus integration). Should reuse the editorial loop's core
interaction pattern (diagnose -> steer -> options -> apply -> verify,
findings as signal not verdicts) and schema conventions (stable finding
ids, spans/regions, rationale) wherever the artifact difference allows
it, and should land inside the same portable CLI/SDK PPY-639fb3 is
building rather than becoming a second, separate tool that happens to
share the Limatus name.
